set.containers.desc: Local addresses and HTTPS for your containers
ctr.title: Containers
ctr.offline: Docker isn't running on this machine. Start Docker and NoCapOS connects on its own.
ctr.search: Search by name, image, project, port or address
ctr.sort.name: Sort: Name
ctr.none: No containers yet. Install an app from the App Store and it appears here.
ctr.killMsg: Kill stops it at once, without letting it save or shut down cleanly.
ctr.proj.stopMsg: All of its containers stop. You can start them again at any time.
ctr.proj.removeMsg: Its containers are removed. Volumes and folders are kept. A saved stack keeps its compose file, so it can be started again.
ctr.proj.fail: The action on {name} did not complete
ctr.proj.stackStarted: {name}: the stack is working on it; see Stacks for progress
ctr.sizeHint: Disk space the container has written
ctr.editStack: Part of the stack {name}: edit its compose file
ctr.updateHint: Download the image again and recreate the container if it changed
ctr.updateMsg: NoCapOS downloads {image} again. If there is a newer image, the container is recreated with it, keeping its settings and data.
ctr.removeFolders: Folders on the server that it used are never touched.
ctr.removeVolumesToo: Also delete its volumes (data stored only in Docker volumes is lost permanently)
ctr.localNone: None: it needs a web port, or local addresses are turned off in Settings
ctr.webHint: Containers on a macvlan or ipvlan network open at their own address automatically. Set an address here when the app is behind a reverse proxy or a name like https://media.home.lan.
ctr.envHint: Values that look like passwords, tokens or keys are hidden. Edit the container to change them.
ctr.hostNet: Uses the server's own network (host mode).
ctr.cmd.hint: Run one command inside the container (sh -c, up to one minute). For longer work, open a full terminal.
ctr.cmd.notRunning: Start the container to run commands in it.
ctr.cmd.label: Command
ctr.files.badName: {name} cannot be uploaded with that name
ctr.files.badPath: Invalid path: it must start with / and cannot contain ..
ctr.files.truncated: Large folder: only the first part is shown.
ctr.files.binary: This is a binary file. It can't be previewed, but it can be downloaded.
ctr.files.previewCut: Only the first 1 MB is shown.
ctr.img.untagMsg: Only this name is removed; the image keeps its other names.
ctr.img.removeMsg: The image is deleted from this server. It can be downloaded again at any time.
ctr.img.pruneMsg: {n} images that no container uses are deleted ({size}). They can be downloaded again later.
ctr.vol.removeMsg: Everything stored in it is lost permanently.
ctr.vol.pruneMsg: Anonymous volumes that no container uses are deleted, with their data.
ctr.vol.pruneNamed: Include named volumes too ({n} unused in total): their data is lost permanently
ctr.dev.hint: USB and serial devices connected to this server (Zigbee sticks, 3D printers, UPS cables…). Attaching one recreates the container with --device.
ctr.dev.none: No USB or serial devices are connected.
ctr.dev.flagHint: What the container gets: the stable name on the server, then the name inside
ctr.dev.attachHint: You review the changes before anything is applied. Containers in a stack get devices from their compose file.
ctr.dev.editorNote: Adding the device {flag}. Review and apply to recreate the container with it.
ctr.net.disconnectMsg: It will no longer reach the other containers on that network.
ctr.spec.limitsHint: Limits keep one container from using the whole server. Set too low, the app may crash or slow down.
ctr.spec.readOnlyNote: Safer: the app can only write to its volumes and folders. Apps that write elsewhere will fail to start.
ctr.spec.privilegedNote: High risk: the container gets full access to the server, like root. Only enable it if the app requires it.
ctr.spec.capsNote: Extra Linux capabilities. Add only what the app's documentation asks for.
ctr.spec.capsHighRisk: Warning: one of these is nearly as powerful as privileged mode.
ctr.spec.devicesHint: Devices from the server (e.g. /dev/dri for a GPU, or a serial port)
ctr.la.title: Local addresses
ctr.la.hint: Every container with a web interface gets a name on your home network, such as http://media.nocap.local. Only devices on your local network can open them.
ctr.la.trustHint: Install NoCapOS's certificate on your devices once and every https:// local address is trusted. It can only vouch for names under nocap.local, never for other websites.
ctr.la.noHttps: This server is not serving HTTPS, so local addresses open over http://.
ctr.la.caHint: nocapos-local-ca.crt: open it on each device and mark it as trusted
ctr.la.notAnnounced: Not announced: turn on the Shield DNS blocker or install Avahi so devices can find these names
ctr.la.empty: No running container has a web port yet.
ctr.la.src.label: {name} (chosen with a label)
ctr.la.customHint: Add these labels to a container to choose its name and which port opens. Use lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, with up to 3 parts.
